Pd/Brønsted Acid Co-catalyzed Dehydrative Coupling of Propargylic
Alcohols with Diarylphosphine Oxides
Zhaoqiang Chen and Hui Qian*
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2025, 27, 522−527

ABSTRACT: An eficient dehydrative coupling of propargylic
alcohols with diarylphosphine oxides to construct tetrasubstituted
allenylphosphoryl compounds in the presence of a Pd/Brønsted
acid co-catalyst has been developed. As a benefit from the use of a
Brønsted acid, this reaction could perform under mild conditions
with excellent yields, accommodating a wide range of functional
groups. The potential utility of this method has also been
demonstrated.

In summary, we have developed an eficient strategy for the
dehydrative coupling to produce the corresponding tetrasub-
stituted allenylphosphoryl products. The key to our protocol
mainly relies on the introduction of Brønsted acid to enhance
the leaving ability of the hydroxyl group, which makes the
reaction work well under mild conditions with better substrate
compatibility. Further studies are currently ongoing in our
laboratory.

In summary, we have developed an eficient strategy for the
dehydrative coupling to produce the corresponding tetrasub-
stituted allenylphosphoryl products. The key to our protocol
mainly relies on the introduction of Brønsted acid to enhance
the leaving ability of the hydroxyl group, which makes the
reaction work well under mild conditions with better substrate
compatibility. Further studies are currently ongoing in our
laboratory.
